membershipRule: implementation-identity: a path belongs to `sources` if and only if its text AT `sourceCommit` was hashed into the sealed implementation digest in src/SIR.Simulation/CombatRules.fs. This list is a historical provenance record of one immutable commit, not an assertion about the current working tree, so it does not change when the tree changes. Most listed paths host no rule symbol, which is intended: the digest fingerprints the runtime-artifact set behind registered algorithms, and over-inclusion is sanctioned while under-inclusion is prohibited. The set is FROZEN at sourceCommit and cannot grow in the change that creates a file: sourceCommit must already be an ancestor of the canonical default branch, and the sealed digest is computed from each listed path's blob AT sourceCommit, so a path a pull request creates has no blob to seal and is refused. Code extracted out of a listed file into a new one is therefore NOT covered by correspondence until sourceCommit is next advanced, which is a deliberate rebind of this immutable half. That loss is not silent: scripts/verify-rules-corpus.sh computes the RULES IMPLEMENTATION CLOSURE -- every project compiling a listed path, plus every project reachable from one of those through ProjectReference, transitively -- and refuses any compile item that entered that closure after sourceCommit unless it is recorded in source-correspondence.json .outsideIdentity. So an extraction is either kept inside a listed file or declared, reviewably, in the diff. The transitive walk is the point: a one-hop version of this check saw 9 projects of 25, and code extracted into a NEW project referenced from a listed path's project passed every gate byte-identically to a clean tree (S.I.R.#290).
workingTreeCorrespondence: tests/fixtures/rules-corpus/v2/source-correspondence.json records the per-path digest the CURRENT tree must still match, and is rebound by scripts/rebind-rules-corpus-sources.sh in the same commit as a reviewed source change. Changing `.sources`, `sourceCommit`, `packageSha256` or `algorithmFingerprint` in THIS file is a deliberate identity rebind that re-seals the implementation digest and regenerates the corpus fixtures. Editing the prose fields alone does NOT: it re-binds only this file's recorded content digest in readiness/198-rules-governance-receipts/evidence-bindings.json and the three receipts derived from it, leaving sourceCommit, the sealed digest, manifest.json, coverage.json and representative-application.hex byte-identical. The earlier wording said changing this file at all re-seals identity, which overstated the blast radius of a documentation fix (S.I.R.#290). See docs/executable-rules-corpus-architecture.md.
